$comment: Classification of Cloudflare/Vercel workspaces. Checked by tools/check-workers.mjs. railsBacked: OpenNext apps that fetch from Rails — they own a src/lib/rails-client.ts copy and declare the VPC binding at the top level (which IS production), in env.development and in env.vpc; env.test carries none. contentSurface: OpenNext apps that do not talk to Rails and must carry no VPC binding at all. standalone: Hono apex workers, no Rails. external: hosted outside Cloudflare, no wrangler config; empty since dev/acme was removed and dev/apex moved onto Workers.
$vpcDevelopmentServiceIdComment: The development VPC Service, bound to the development tunnel (1d501e9a-62f7-4c0d-ba5e-a26e3f10088f) and terminating on <frame>.<brand>.localhost:3000. Verify with `wrangler vpc service get <id>`.
$vpcProductionServiceIdComment: BOOTSTRAP: equal to vpcDevelopmentServiceId on purpose. AWS production Rails and a production tunnel do not exist yet, so the deployed production Worker exercises the real edge → Workers VPC → VPC Service → tunnel → Rails path against local Rails. This field is the AWS cutover point: provision the production VPC Service, change this id and the fifteen top-level service_ids, and the two stop being equal. No application code changes. See adr/006-development-workers-vpc-transport.md.
